summary: Thurston County, NE steel-frame tower on the Winnebago Reservation, completed in August 1937 per a Nov 1937 newspaper story; listed gone and removed, with no removal date or present-day description found.

facts.design: steel-frame outlook tower with a crow's nest 70 feet above the ground, on a high bluff over the Missouri River
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it 'Removed'; Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as 'Tower Gone'; no removal date found

staffing.status: Leland Decora, 31, a Winnebago Indian, was boss of the tower and spent eight hours a day in the crow's nest; reported by telephone to the agency at Winnebago (1937 article)

facts.agency: Winnebago Indian Reservation; the 1937 article says a delegation of twelve councilmen of the Winnebago tribe controlled the forestry project

events.note: Sunday Journal and Star story dated November 7, 1937 says the first of a series of government-built towers in Thurston County was completed in August; the year is inferred from the article date and the tower was built under a 'CC-ID Indian division project'
Leland Decora, 31, named boss of the tower in the 1937 article
